title: DeckTalk per-machine settings file
description: The keys a per-machine settings file may hold, which are the ones that describe this machine rather than the film. A key about the film belongs in the project file, because the file that ships carries whatever the runner believes.

narration.description: These keys govern how the script is turned into audio.

concurrency.description: How many sections `narrate` voices at once.
concurrency.x-hazard: A voice provider limits requests per account, and a busy answer is retried rather than paid twice.

retries.description: How many more times `narrate` asks again when the voice provider or the aligner answers that it is busy or failed.

store_dir.description: The take store: a folder outside every project where this machine keeps a second copy of every voiced take it makes and its provider words, each named by its digest. A take is looked for here after `takes_dir`, and one found here is checked and copied into `takes_dir`, so a deck with the same words as another plays it without buying it, and a take nobody committed yet survives a `git clean`. Each take is written here once, and a store that already holds a good copy keeps it. It is empty for the `takes` folder in the per-user data folder, such as `~/Library/Application Support/decktalk/takes` on macOS.
store_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type
store_dir.x-hazard: It holds the spoken words of every script voiced on this machine, so keep it out of a synced or shared folder. A relative path, a folder inside the project or one inside the tool cache is refused when the project loads. Write an absolute path or one that starts with ~.

store_wait_seconds.description: Seconds a run waits while another run on this machine voices the same take into the take store, before it is refused as locked. Keep it above one whole take request, `timeout_seconds` times `retries` plus one, with the waits between them. The default covers that at the default `timeout_seconds` and `retries`: four attempts of 180 seconds and three waits of at most 30 seconds, 810 seconds.
store_wait_seconds.x-hazard: Below the length of one take request, a run is refused while another run's healthy request is still being answered.

record.description: These keys tune how `record` opens each page section in headless Chromium and steps it frame by frame.

page_policy.description: How far `record`, `check` and `storyboard` trust a page. `trusted` lets a page reach the network as a browser would. `untrusted` turns the Chromium sandbox on and refuses every request that is not for the project's own origin, through every channel a page can open. It is the machine's to set, so a project someone else wrote cannot trust its own page.
page_policy.x-range: must be one of trusted, untrusted
page_policy.x-hazard: A service that renders pages other people wrote sets `untrusted` on its machine, because a trusted page can reach anything the machine can, including a cloud metadata endpoint.

concurrency.description: How many page sections `record` records at once. Zero chooses from the CPU this process may use, which inside a container is its quota rather than the host's core count.
concurrency.x-hazard: Each recording steps its own Chromium and its own encode, so a number above the machine's share makes every section wait on the others and the run slower rather than faster.

capture_switches.description: Chromium switches `record` launches its browser with, which stop it holding its frames to the display's refresh rate, so a recorded frame takes about half the time. A recording with them decodes to the same frames as one without them. An empty list launches Chromium with none.
capture_switches.x-range: must hold values that each must be one of disable-frame-rate-limit, disable-gpu-vsync
capture_switches.x-hazard: With the switches no frame waits for a display refresh, so each recording keeps more of the CPU busy, and a `record.concurrency` set by hand above the machine's share makes the sections wait on each other.

frame_wait_seconds.description: Longest `record` waits for a page to draw one stepped frame, with every font it shows loaded, every image decoded and the step laid out and painted, before it fails the section rather than capture the frame half drawn.
frame_wait_seconds.x-range: must be above 0 and must be at most 120
frame_wait_seconds.x-hazard: A wait too short for this machine fails sections whose pages are only slow to fetch a font or decode an image. It never shortens a recording that succeeds, because a page that has drawn its frame is captured at once.

skip_audit_every.description: Step to and capture every this many frames `record` writes again anyway, and stop the section if one differs from the frame before. Zero audits none, which is the fast path, and the test suite sets it to prove the frames written again.
skip_audit_every.x-hazard: Every audited frame costs one step and one capture, so one audits every skipped frame and saves no time.

elevenlabs.description: These keys are ElevenLabs's own: its speech fields, its model, its rate, its output format and its API. The key it is bought with is `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `base_url` is the machine's to set. The score stage buys from the same API with the same key.

base_url.description: Base URL of the ElevenLabs API, which the voice and the score both send their requests and the key to.
base_url.x-range: takes any value of its type
base_url.x-hazard: The script, and for a provider that bills the API key, travels to whatever host this names, so only the machine names it and a project file that sets it is refused.

dtsp.description: These keys are the `dtsp` provider's own: where its local server listens, the model it reads with, and how long the server has to say which aligner it serves. `dtsp` speaks the DeckTalk speech protocol to `decktalk-voice`, a separate local server that is not part of this repository. The same server times the words of a take whose voice sent none. It needs no key, bills nothing, and `base_url` is the machine's to set.

base_url.description: Base URL of decktalk-voice, the local server that reads the script for `dtsp` and times the words of a take that came without them. Port 9361 is assigned to nothing at IANA and listed in no /etc/services, so no other service is expected to answer there.
base_url.x-range: takes any value of its type
base_url.x-hazard: The script, and for a provider that bills the API key, travels to whatever host this names, so only the machine names it and a project file that sets it is refused.

handshake_seconds.description: Seconds the local server has to say which aligner it serves, asked at most once per run and only when a take has no aligned words kept. It is short because a server that is up answers at once, so a port held by a process that never answers costs this wait and not `[narration] timeout_seconds`.

events.description: These keys bound the events files a run writes under `build/events/`.

max_bytes.description: Bytes one run's events file may reach before progress lines, download lines and debug and info lines are left out of it. Warnings and errors are left out once it reaches twice this. Lines about the run, its stages, its sections, its findings and its costs are always kept.
max_bytes.x-hazard: A file with no bound grows with every tool call a long film makes, on a disk a host shares.

tools.description: These keys name the tools DeckTalk drives, for a machine that supplies its own.

chromium.description: Chromium executable that `record`, `check` and `storyboard` drive. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself, and a path here is what a managed machine sets: a named executable that will not launch is never a reason to download another.
chromium.x-range: takes any value of its type

ffmpeg.description: ffmpeg executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffmpeg.x-range: takes any value of its type

ffprobe.description: ffprobe executable. It is empty for the build DeckTalk fetches itself.
ffprobe.x-range: takes any value of its type

timeout_seconds.description: Longest one ffmpeg or ffprobe call, or one wait on another fetch of ffmpeg, may run before it is stopped.

cache_dir.description: Directory the fetched Chromium and ffmpeg builds live in, Chromium in its ms-playwright folder. It is empty for the standard per-user cache.
cache_dir.x-range: takes any value of its type
cache_dir.x-hazard: A relative path is refused when the machine loads. Write an absolute path or one that starts with ~.
